function: Sensing-assisted channel prediction: forecasts the next Q=5 slots of communication CSI from the previous P=10 slots of communication and sensing CSI in an ISAC OFDM system (pp. 2-4).
system: ISAC BS with 4x4 dual-polarized half-wavelength UPA, user with one omnidirectional antenna, OFDM at 28 GHz, 5.76 MHz bandwidth, 48 subcarriers at 60 kHz; no RIS (p. 4).
method: Pre-trained GPT-2 backbone (attention and feed-forward frozen; addition, layer-norm, positional layers fine-tuned) with ConvLSTM channel attention and cross-attention fusion; supervised, NMSE loss (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own Sionna ray-tracing dataset of a street scene with moving vehicles (LoS, reflection, scattering) plus applied Doppler shifts; 6000 training and 600 test samples; no release stated (p. 4).
test_conditions: One street scene, 6000 training and 600 test samples; speed 10-100 km/h evaluated per speed (Fig. 4); SNR sweep, trained at 0-25 dB (Fig. 5) (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: LSTM, Transformer [4], CNN; scheme without sensing assistance (communication CSI only, type not specified); ablations without channel attention, cross-attention, LLM; no classical predictor (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE of predicted communication CSI versus user speed (Fig. 4), versus SNR of noisy historical CSI (Fig. 5), and in ablation (Table I) (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "is generated using the Sionna platform" with ray tracing of a specified street geometry, and p. 4: "shifts are applied to all paths to simulate the time variation of" the channels; a self-generated dataset, not 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "The dataset contains 6000 training samples and 600 test samples" from one street scene; p. 5: "the SNR is set to be uniformly distributed between 0 and 25 dB" in training. Speed and SNR sweeps stay within the training conditions; no new scene, configuration, band, or site is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "several commonly adopted deep learning-based channel prediction methods as baselines" (LSTM, Transformer [4], CNN) plus a no-sensing scheme; no non-learned predictor is compared, and the statistical method [2] of the introduction is not tested.
q4_support: p. 3: "to reduce the computational complexity for training, we implement the parallel processing" is only qualitative; no order of complexity, operations, parameters, or runtime is reported in the paper.
q5_support: p. 4: "is generated using the Sionna platform" for a self-built street scene; no code or data link is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used. Sionna is an open-source library [13], but the dataset and the code are not released.
notes: Area 2: sensing-assisted channel prediction in an ISAC system is channel prediction (area 2); the output is predicted CSI, not beams, waveforms, or resources (area 5). q1 is 0 because the dataset is self-generated with Sionna ray tracing in an unnamed street scene with Doppler shifts added (p. 4), not 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data; the reviewer may check whether Sionna ray tracing counts as widely shared. q3 is 0 because every compared predictor is learned; the no-sensing scheme is described only as using communication CSI (p. 4) and appears as W/o sensing in the ablation (Table I, p. 5). Historical CSI is assumed perfectly known (footnote 2, p. 3). The file is the arXiv preprint v1 of 14 May 2025 (arXiv:2505.09141v1); the DOI is not printed in the file.
